title: Adversarial autoencoder predicts cellular morphology from gene expression across donors
summary: An adversarially aligned autoencoder trained on four perturbation datasets predicted cell morphology from gene expression and generalized without retraining to RNA-seq and cell painting profiles from 100 genetically diverse iPSC donors. Seventeen morphological features were strongly predicted, with the signal spread across many genes rather than a few. Independent CRISPR perturbations supported model-prioritized genes including TIAM1, RAB31 and ABCC5, while genetic analyses linked PDHX, SLC11A2 and MAPKAPK5 variants to morphology.
ai_technology: Adversarially aligned autoencoder for cross-modal prediction of morphology from gene expression

evidence.tested: Independent CRISPR perturbations of model-prioritized genes, and held-out donor RNA-seq and cell painting data.
evidence.unknown: How many prioritized genes were confirmed, and the causal role of the genetic associations; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: An autoencoder predicted cell painting features from transcriptomes and prioritized genes.
